groups.name: TV shows widely celebrated for ending on the creator's own terms
groups.explanation: Babylon 5 (JMS planned a 5-season arc from the start), The Prisoner (Patrick McGoohan's fiercely personal finale), Halt and Catch Fire (AMC, creators ended it exactly as they envisioned), and Six Feet Under (Alan Ball's planned series finale is frequently cited as one of the greatest in TV history) all ended deliberately on the creator's terms rather than through cancellation or network interference.

groups.name: Fictional TV locations that are also the name of a real place in a different country
groups.explanation: Waystar (Waystar Royco, Succession) is a real village in Cornwall, England; Wentworth is a real village in South Yorkshire, England (and a golf club in Virginia, USA); The Bear is a real pub name common across England; Agrestic is a real comune in Italy (Agrestic does not exist — REBUILDING NEEDED).

groups.name: TV characters whose first name is shared by a Harry Potter character
groups.explanation: ALMA Garrett (Deadwood) shares her first name with Alma Dumbledore (Harry Potter); SHIV Roy — Shiv is not an HP name; TOM Ripley shares his first name with Tom Riddle (Voldemort); KIMMY Schmidt — not HP. This still does not work cleanly.

groups.name: Tiles that are actually Harry Potter characters used as TV character tiles
groups.explanation: Padma Patil, Melisandre, Fleabag, Cordell Walker — this grouping is arbitrary and does not work.
